page: UpCloud HICPU-64xCPU-96GB is a compute-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system allocates 64 physical cores with a single thread per core, utilizing a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity is configured at 96.0 GB, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 1.5 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 200 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is positioned in the bottom 10%, reflecting the lower clock speed and shared CPU allocation. However, multi-threaded capabilities are robust, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, Geekbench ray tracing, and Passmark CPU metrics all scoring in the top 25%. Redis SET operations also demonstrate strong performance, reaching 61.57 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth remains average across both small and large block read/write tests.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers high compute density with a massive core count, making it highly suitable for parallelizable workloads that do not require high memory-per-core ratios. The low memory allocation relative to the 64 vCPUs represents a tradeoff for memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for multi-threaded processing tasks, software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput Redis caching, while being less optimal for single-threaded applications or large-scale LLM inference.
